brief.headline: Push for early-payment discount and formally qualify Tirupati or Gulshan as second source to reduce single-supplier risk on a ₹15.03 Cr spend

priceAsk.summary: Hold current price and explore small discount for faster payment — our ₹66.48/KG is already market-fair
priceAsk.target: ₹66.48/KG current price; benchmark to market ask typical band ₹66–73/kg
priceAsk.basis: We are already at the best price we pay anyone. Market ask shows ₹60–81/kg band, typical ₹66–73/kg — verdict is MARKET-FAIR (slightly favourable). India export reference sits at 42.95 ₹/kg. Our price is fair; the win is on payment terms and second-sourcing, not a big price cut.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Ask to pay 15 days faster (45 days total from receipt) in exchange for a small discount, freeing up ₹61.76 L in cash for us
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹61.76 L cash freed up for us by paying 15 days faster

brief.financialLeverage: Sayaji publishes no financials, so we can't see how healthy or cash-tight they are. Our ₹15.03 Cr annual spend gives us meaningful volume to negotiate with. Without their numbers, we lean on our own data (we're already at the best price we pay) and on the fact that three listed alternates — Tirupati, Gulshan, Sanstar — make the exact same anhydrous dextrose. That competitive backdrop means we can ask for faster payment terms in return for a discount, and we should actively qualify a second source to protect supply and keep pricing honest.

evidence.point: We spend ₹15.03 Cr annually with Sayaji — a meaningful volume for leverage
Our current average price is ₹66.48/KG, already the best price we pay anyone for Dextrose
Market ask for Anhydrous Dextrose IP is ₹60–81/kg (typical ₹66–73/kg) — our price lands in the typical band, verdict MARKET-FAIR (slightly favourable)
Paying 15 days faster would free up ₹61.76 L in cash for us
Current payment terms are 30 Days After Receipt — not the worst, but room to negotiate for a discount if we speed up
Three listed alternates (Tirupati, Gulshan, Sanstar) are established dextrose makers — credible second sources to reduce dependence on a single supplier
evidence.figure: Tirupati Starch & Chemicals Ltd, Gulshan Polyols Ltd, Sanstar Ltd

alternates.name: Tirupati Starch & Chemicals Ltd
alternates.why: Listed Indore maize wet-miller; makes Dextrose ANHYDROUS (IV-fluid grade) — exact form match; confirm IP monograph CoA before switching

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed starch & polyol maker; established dextrose/sorbitol supplier — a drop-in alternate to Gujarat Ambuja/Sayaji

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist (starch, dextrose) — growing capacity

risks: Sayaji's financials aren't public — we can't see cash health or stability, so monitor supply continuity closely and don't rely on them alone
We already pay the best price (₹66.48/KG, 0.0% gap), so there's little room for a big price cut — focus the ask on payment-term discount and second-sourcing instead
Three listed alternates exist but none are yet qualified — we need to start RFQs and audits now to have a real backup if Sayaji stumbles or plays hard on terms
Roquette India (₹2898.05 Cr revenue, global pedigree) is premium and very reliable, but likely pricier — use as escalation option if Sayaji or the listed trio can't meet quality or delivery
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership and our ₹15 crore annual Dextrose spend with you — today I'd like to discuss a faster payment schedule in exchange for a small discount, and also explore how we jointly plan for capacity and continuity as our volumes grow.
